newsitem.title: USA: Vallejo, Calif., council to assume park ownership.
newsitem.headline: Vallejo, Calif., council to assume park ownership.

text.p: The Vallejo, Calif., city council adopted a resolution to take over the Marine World Africa USA theme park and assume about $52 million of its long-term debt, city officials said on Wednesday.
The city council adopted a resolution creating the Marine World Joint Powers Authority, with council members serving as the authority's board of directors.
Effective November 1, the non-profit Marine World Foundation will transfer ownership of Marine World facilities, animals and assets to the joint powers authority, city officials said.
Marine World Africa USA does not have the funds to fully repay its short-term noteholders, the city said, estimating that the park was short more than $2 million due November 1.
The city said, however, that noteholders would be paid in full because city funds would be used to offset the shortfall.
The park also has about $52 million of long-term debt, which was backed by Vallejo. The city will assume those obligations, Vallejo City Manager Kenneth Campo said.
The city decided to take over the park because of declining revenues and attendance. Attendance has fallen about 19 percent since 1995, when some 1.6 million visited the park.
Park spokesman Jeff Jouett said the city plans to provide funds to the park to build new attractions to boost lagging attendance.

The theme park has 1,300 employees during the summer season and about 500 employees year-round. None of these jobs are at risk in the shift to city ownership, Jouett said. The theme park is the largest private employer in the city.
"We know what to do to make Marine World work," Jouett said. "Any new funding for new attractions should put us right back in the thick of tourism competition in San Francisco."
Campo estimated that it would take the city two to three years to make Marine World economically viable for sale.
The city will work with private companies that may be interested in buying, investing in or managing the park, he said. City officials said they would also consider restructuring the park's debt.
